attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The added phrase about supplying compute follows from his next sentence ('they need cloud compute'). It keeps 'in essence' and adds no claim about revenue share or equal economics.

contract.note: Reading it as a comparison of supplier roles is the ordinary reading of a qualitative analogy. The contract does not require equal revenue or a share driven by experimentation, which matches his words. The target window covers the last reported quarters before the post.

evidence.note: April 2024 AWS/Slack account: Slack's AI features run on AWS GPU instances. This is a documented customer deployment of AWS compute for AI. It is a company disclosure.
NVIDIA's release for the quarter ended July 28, 2024 reports record data-center revenue and strong Hopper demand driven by generative AI. It was published before the post.
Amazon's Q2 2024 call reports significant demand for its training and inference chips and NVIDIA instances, which is AWS supplying AI compute.
Amazon Q is an application-layer product, so AWS AI is more than raw compute. That limits stronger readings but does not show the analogy rests on a false description.

reviews.rationale: Disclosures from the target period show customers using AWS compute for AI (Slack on GPU instances, demand for AWS chips) and strong demand for NVIDIA compute products. That meets the support condition for the supplier-role analogy. Amazon's application-layer products are context only; they do not make his description of AWS materially false.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his newsletter. The OpenAI figures are exceptions he states himself and are not graded here.

semantics.note: 'This' refers to cloud-provider revenue growth from organisations' own AI integrations. The normalisation keeps both of his exceptions and 'alleged', and adds no threshold.

contract.note: The result depends on reading the OpenAI exception as covering only OpenAI's own revenue, not Azure AI services. That is an ordinary reading, because Azure revenue belongs to Microsoft. No dollar threshold is imposed, which matches his unqualified 'yet to see'.

evidence.note: Microsoft's call for the quarter ended June 30, 2024 (held July 30, 2024) says 8 points of Azure growth came from AI services. That is realized growth for a cloud provider other than AWS, reported before the post.
The release confirms the period ended June 30, 2024. It is used only to check timing.

reviews.rationale: Before the post, Microsoft publicly attributed 8 points of Azure revenue growth in the April–June 2024 quarter to AI services. That is realized cloud-provider revenue growth from AI outside his two exceptions, which meets the contradiction condition. The disclosure does not isolate customer-built integrations, but AI services sold to customers fall within the ordinary reading.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps 'I can find no', 'appears' and the Microsoft exception. The phrasing is firm, not hedged, so it is a scorable observation.

contract.note: The contract reads 'I can find no' as a claim about the public record and counts Palantir as a public SaaS company because it sells hosted subscriptions. Both are evaluator interpretations, but ordinary ones. 'Appears to have attributed' sets a low bar for what counts as attribution. The Microsoft parenthetical is treated as context only.

evidence.note: On Palantir's Q2 2024 call (Aug 5, 2024, reproduction identified), management said AIP was driving new and expanded customers, alongside 55% growth in US commercial revenue. That appears to attribute meaningful realized growth to AIP.
The 10-Q reproduction shows Palantir sells hosted software subscriptions and describes AIP as built on generative models, which places Palantir in the company population.
Copilot customers grew more than 60% quarter on quarter. That is adoption, not revenue, and only bears on the Microsoft parenthetical.

reviews.rationale: Before the post, Palantir, a public seller of hosted software, linked growth in new and existing customers to its generative-AI platform AIP while reporting 55% realized growth in US commercial revenue. Under 'appears to have attributed', that is a qualifying counterexample outside Microsoft. Management attribution is not causal proof, but the claim is about attribution. The Microsoft parenthetical is not scored.
